valuation_philosophy.model: Blended NTA exit-P/B (50%) and earnings exit-P/E (50%), five-year horizon, interim dividends, all discounted at the NZD cost of equity. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Land subdivider, inventory-heavy developer'; the same model as CDI.NZ.
valuation_philosophy.why_not_owner_fcf: Winton's reported FCF is inventory timing, not earnings power: FY22-24 FCF was negative (-16, -14, -28) while the company built land bank, FY26 CSV FCF was +$96.5m (OCF 105.9 less PP&E capex 9.4; +$80.1m after investment-property purchases) because a $53.4m inventory run-down (Lakeside bulk settlement to Kainga Ora) converted to cash and repaid the Lakeside and Northlake facilities. Neither is a repeatable base and a Gordon-growth terminal on either is meaningless. Value is instead the land bank (NTA, carried at cost for inventory and fair value for investment property) and the mid-cycle earnings it can generate.
valuation_philosophy.why_not_pure_nav: Half the value is put on NTA because 1.87 cps of book is real (inventories at cost, investment property at IAS 40 fair value, no goodwill), but a pure NAV model ignores that Winton must fund, consent, build and sell that land through a cycle at a ~5% ROE; the earnings leg prices that.
valuation_philosophy.net_debt_treatment: Net debt ($5.4m: $44.2m project-level non-recourse borrowings less $38.8m cash) is NOT subtracted from either exit value. Both legs are equity values (book equity and after-interest NPAT). Subtracting it again would double count. Lease liabilities ($23.5m) and residents' ORA loans ($18.2m) are likewise inside book equity and inside NPAT.
valuation_philosophy.risk_charged_once: Cyclicality, the Sunfield litigation and settlement-volume risk are charged in the scenario NPAT paths and the 30% bear weight. Governance/control, size and illiquidity are charged in the cost of equity. The same 15.5% rate is used in all three scenarios.

inputs.share_count_basis: 296,613,736 ordinary shares (CSV SharesOutstanding, unchanged since the Dec-2021 IPO; FY26 annual report note 10.4). The 10.332m employee options (note 10.12) have a $3.887 weighted exercise price, 3.5x the current price and above every intrinsic value in this model, so treasury-stock dilution is nil; the 306.96m 'diluted' EPS denominator is a simple gross-up and is not used. Count held FLAT: SBC ($1.28m) is expensed inside NPAT.
inputs.debt_note: Borrowings are two project-level facilities (BNZ/Sunfield $25.7m expiring 10-Aug-2027, MCCB/Cracker Bay $18.2m expiring 21-Nov-2027), non-recourse to the group; Lakeside and Northlake facilities repaid June 2026. Weighted rate 8.19%, weighted term 1.2 years. Lease liabilities $23.5m and residents' loans $18.2m excluded from debt (treated as operating; their cost is inside NPAT).
inputs.nta_note: NTA 186.9 cps at 30-Jun-2026 (CSV NTAPerShare; equity $555.4m less $0.96m intangibles over 296.6m shares). Inventories $172.3m at cost (of which only $16.2m 'expected to settle within one year', vs $46.4m a year earlier), investment properties $369.2m at IAS 40 fair value, PP&E (Northbrook, Ayrburn) $110.4m. Price/NTA today 0.59x; the market paid 1.08-1.67x at each June balance date FY22-FY25 and 1.16x at Dec-2025, before the 2026 governance crisis.
inputs.presale_note: Pre-sale book $27.4m at 30-Jun-2026 versus $248.0m at 30-Jun-2025, $239.8m at 31-Dec-2025 and $419.3m at 30-Jun-2023. In every prior listed year the opening book covered the following year's development revenue 1.7-2.6x (Jun-25 $248.0m vs FY26 development revenue $147.8m). FY26's 430 settlements consumed the Lakeside/Kainga Ora contracts (Stage 4 240 lots + Stage 5A 77 lots) and the conclusion of that land-supply agreement removed the balance, so the book did not simply convert: roughly $70m+ of Jun-25 pre-sales were cancelled or re-timed rather than settled. FY27 therefore opens with contracted cover for ~25-40% of the development revenue in the base case, the first year in the listed history without full cover. This is why FY27 NPAT is cut to a gap-year level and FY28 is held below trend in every scenario (v1.1 change).
inputs.last_fcf_note: Not applicable: earnings + NTA model. FY26 CSV FreeCashFlow 96.543 (OCF 105.949 less PP&E CapEx 9.406) and the all-investing figure of 80.1 (also net of investment-property 16.4 and intangibles 0.06 purchases) are both an inventory run-down (-$53.4m), not owner earnings.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: WIN.NZ_Metrics.csv FY2026 FreeCashFlow = OperatingCashFlow 105.949 - CapEx 9.406 (PP&E only). Investment-property purchases of 16.4 are outside the CSV definition; net of them FCF is 80.1 (the v1.0 figure).
inputs.sbc_source: CSV StockBasedComp FY2026 (-1.281; FY26 annual report income statement 'Share-based payment expense' $1,281k, note 10.12; equity-settled options, no cash withholding). Already deducted inside NPAT; street basis adds it back.
inputs.interest_income_note: Inside NPAT and not stripped: cash ($38.8m) is not added to value separately, so there is no double count.
inputs.dividend_note: Dividends paused since FY25; Board 'actively considering how and when it might resume'. Base resumes at 40% payout from FY28 ($5.6m on $14m NPAT, easily funded from $38.8m cash).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-20T22:47:01Z (Yahoo regularMarketTime; 10:47 NZST Monday 21-Sep-2026, live intraday NZX quote, currency NZD; unchanged from v1.0, no later trade printed by the time of the v1.1 update)
inputs.balance_sheet_source: WIN.NZ_Metrics.csv FY2026 row (adjudicated into core_metrics by the financial-parser agent, 21-Sep-2026; source filing WIN.NZ_Annual_FY2026, NZX announcement 478541, 26-Aug-2026, audited). The v1.0 manual anchors taken from the same filing tie to the CSV row exactly on every field used (revenue, EBITDA, NPAT, EPS, equity, cash, debt, shares, SBC, NTA, units).
inputs.notes: MODEL: blended NTA exit-P/B + earnings exit-P/E (dcf-methods routing row 'Land subdivider, inventory-heavy developer'; CDI.NZ precedent). Unchanged from v1.0. Not an owner-FCF DCF, so the dashboard slider engine has no component drivers to rebuild and will fall back to the stored values; that is expected for this model family. UPDATE v1.1 (2026-09-21, same day as the v1.0 fresh build): anchors re-sourced from the now-authoritative WIN.NZ_Metrics.csv FY2026 row (all tie to v1.0; reported_fcf now carries the CSV definition 96.543 instead of the all-investing 80.1, which changes nothing in the valuation). One driver change: FY27 and FY28 NPAT cut in every scenario (bear 5/6 -> -4/3; base 11/18 -> 5/14; bull 15/26 -> 9/22) after weighing the pre-sale history (see presale_note). FY29-31, the $32m base mid-cycle, payout paths, exit multiples, the 15.5% cost of equity and the 30/50/20 weights are deliberately unchanged. Founder Chris Meehan resigned as director effective 14-Sep-2026 but still holds ~55%; Macquarie (TC Akarua) 22.35%; free float ~22%. The audited FY26 accounts disclose no contingent liability, so the media-reported ~$138m Kainga Ora claim is treated as unverified and carried only as bear-case legal drag; the Sunfield High Court appeal (Auckland Council, hearing Sept-2026) is the live litigation and is the main bear axis.

historical_growth.mid_cycle_rationale: Base year-5 NPAT $32m = the FY21-FY26 six-year mean ($31.9m), which spans the FY21-23 post-COVID boom and the FY24-26 downturn. It is ~5.2% ROE on projected FY31 equity, ~1.4x FY26 NPAT and half the FY23 peak. FY26's $22.7m is itself a partial-recovery print inflated by the Lakeside/Kainga Ora bulk settlement (317 lots at $344k average, down from $489k), and FY27 has almost no pre-sale cover, so the path dips before it recovers. Unchanged in v1.1.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: NTA compounding: mid-cycle ROE ~5.2% net of a 40% payout, cross-checked against the FY22-26 equity CAGR of 5.2% (FY21 base is pre-IPO and unusable; the Dec-2021 IPO raised equity from $84m to $423m).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR +2.9% vs EPS 3yr CAGR -29.5% and revenue 3yr CAGR -3.7%: FY23 was the settlement peak (565 units) and FY26 a partial recovery from the FY25/H1 FY26 trough (266 units, then 14 in H1 FY26). No trailing CAGR describes the forward business; mid-cycle normalisation is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs deliberately null: reported FCF flips sign with inventory build/run-down (FY22 -16.1, FY23 -14.3, FY24 -27.8, FY25 +22.8, FY26 +96.5 on the CSV definition) and is not an earnings series. All history now read from WIN.NZ_Metrics.csv.

wacc_rationale.build: Risk-free 4.4% (NZ Government 10-year, Sept-2026, assumed) + beta 1.2 x NZ equity risk premium 5.5% = 11.0% (NZ small-cap developer base); + 2.0pp size/illiquidity (market cap ~NZ$330m, ~22% free float, ASX/NZX quotation suspended 31-Aug to 3-Sep-2026); + 2.5pp governance/control/key-person premium (55% controlling holder rejected proposed minority-protection constitutional amendments; independent Chair, independent director, CEO, CFO, general counsel and a senior executive all departed between July and September 2026; new Chair appointed 2-Sep-2026 without a permanent CEO). Total 15.5%. Unchanged in v1.1.
wacc_rationale.not_charged_here: Cyclicality, project concentration and the Sunfield litigation are charged in the scenario NPAT paths, exit multiples and the 30% bear weight, not in the rate (owner-fcf.md section 7f, charge risk once). Same rate in all scenarios.
wacc_rationale.comparison: CDI.NZ (same model) uses 17.0% including 1.5pp cyclicality and 0.75pp land concentration in the rate; WIN charges those through the flows instead, hence 15.5%.

bear.narrative: FY27 loss: the $27.4m opening pre-sale book plus $16.2m of 'within one year' inventory (at cost) is all the booked cover there is; in-year sales are thin, the High Court quashes the Sunfield consent (or remits it for years), the Auckland market stays subdued, legal and restructuring costs run through FY27-28 and the board/majority-holder standoff recurs. NPAT -$4m in FY27 (~$90m revenue: ~$45m hospitality/other floor plus ~$45m development) and $3m in FY28, then recovering only to ~$15m by FY31 (FY24 level); no dividend until FY30, exit P/B 0.55x (a step below today's 0.59x) and exit P/E 8x. Not modelled: a Sunfield inventory impairment if the consent is quashed; that would hit the NTA leg directly.

base.narrative: FY27 is a gap year: the $248.0m Jun-25 pre-sale book (which covered FY26's $147.8m development revenue 1.7x) was consumed and partly cancelled when the Kainga Ora land-supply agreement concluded, leaving $27.4m at 30-Jun-26 against a hospitality/other revenue floor of ~$45m. FY27 revenue ~$110m (development ~$65m: $27m contracted plus in-year Northlake/Lakeside/Launch Bay lot sales) and NPAT ~$5m (gross profit ~$58m less ~$46m opex, $7.5m D&A, $2.5m net interest, plus a small revaluation gain); FY28 ~$14m as the pipeline sold during FY27 settles and Goodfellows (sales campaign Oct-26) / Northbrook Stage 2 (opens 2027) begin contributing. From FY29 the path is unchanged: earnings rebuild to a ~$32m mid-cycle by FY31 (6-year FY21-26 average $31.9m; ~5.2% ROE). Sunfield survives the Auckland Council High Court appeal but contributes little inside the horizon. Dividend resumes at ~40% payout from FY28. Exit P/B 0.80x: partial repair of the governance discount (0.59x today) but below the 1.1-1.2x the market paid in FY24-25 before the crisis; exit P/E 11x on mid-cycle earnings.

bull.narrative: FY27 is still thin (NPAT ~$9m on ~$125m revenue: even a strong market cannot settle what was not pre-sold at 30-Jun-26), then the cycle turns: unemployment peaks in 2027, Queenstown-Lakes stays strong, FY28 NPAT ~$22m; Sunfield's fast-track consent is upheld and first stages settle FY29-31; Goodfellows and Northbrook scale ORA income; the Stiassny board lands a credible CEO and the majority holder either accepts minority protections or sells down. NPAT reaches ~$50m by FY31 (FY21 level, below the FY23 peak of $64.6m; ~7.8% ROE), payout 50% from FY28, exit P/B 1.05x (back to the FY24-25 regime) and exit P/E 13x.

bear.fcf_note: Not projected: reported FCF for a land developer is inventory timing (FY26 +$96.5m on a $53.4m inventory run-down; FY22-24 negative on land-bank build). Value is derived from NPAT and NTA, not FCF.

base.fcf_note: Not projected: reported FCF for a land developer is inventory timing (FY26 +$96.5m on a $53.4m inventory run-down; FY22-24 negative on land-bank build). Value is derived from NPAT and NTA, not FCF.

bull.fcf_note: Not projected: reported FCF for a land developer is inventory timing (FY26 +$96.5m on a $53.4m inventory run-down; FY22-24 negative on land-bank build). Value is derived from NPAT and NTA, not FCF.

entry_price.methodology: Price at which PV(FY27-31 dividends at 15%) + PV(year-5 blended exit value at 15%) returns a 15% IRR. Exit multiples are the same P/B and P/E as the scenario's own (a 15%-hurdle buyer and the 15.5% cost-of-equity buyer are the same buyer within rounding), so the entry price sits marginally ABOVE intrinsic value in every scenario; that is the CDI.NZ mirror pattern, not a bug. Net debt is inside book equity and NPAT and is not added.

required_return_table.note: Each column rediscounts the year-5 blended exit value and the dividends at that rate; exit multiples held at the base 0.80x P/B / 11x P/E. The 15% column equals entry_price.base; the 15.5% column equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value. Price of $1.11 implies a required return of roughly 8-9% on the base path.

sensitivity.note: Not a Gordon-growth model: axes are cost of equity and the year-5 exit P/B (exit P/E scaled proportionally, 11x at 0.80x). Base scenario. Centre cell = valuation.base.intrinsic_value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30% (up from the 15% house default): FY27 has almost no pre-sale cover, the Sunfield consent is before the High Court in Sept-2026, the shareholder-level governance dispute is unresolved (the 55% holder declined minority protections and has just left the board, which removes a distraction but not the control), and the company has no permanent CEO or CFO. Bull 20% (down from 35%): it needs a housing-cycle turn, a Sunfield win and a governance normalisation, three largely independent events. Base 50%. Unchanged in v1.1.
probability_weighted.band_note: Set to null: the street basis only adds back $1.28m/yr of option expense, so house and street weighted IVs differ by 1.7c (0.7475 vs 0.7649) and the $1.11 price sits ~21 band-widths above both. A percentage inside that band is degenerate; the finding is simply that the price is far above either SBC treatment.

Driver change, bear FY27/28 NPAT 5/6 -> -4/3: year-5 NTA -4.0c x 0.55 P/B x DF 0.4865 x 50% blend; no dividend effect (payout 0 until FY30); scenario IV -0.54c x 30% weight
Driver change, base FY27/28 NPAT 11/18 -> 5/14: year-5 NTA -2.8c x 0.80 P/B x DF x 50% (-0.55c) plus FY28 dividend 7.2m -> 5.6m (-0.40c PV); scenario IV -0.96c x 50% weight
Driver change, bull FY27/28 NPAT 15/26 -> 9/22: year-5 NTA -2.7c x 1.05 P/B x DF x 50% (-0.69c) plus FY28 dividend 13.0m -> 11.0m (-0.51c PV); scenario IV -1.19c x 20% weight

deliberately_unchanged.fy29_to_fy31_npat_paths: Unchanged in all scenarios; the pre-sale evidence bears on FY27 (settlements of contracts already signed) and FY28 (settlements of contracts signed during FY27), not on the mid-cycle. Would move on: the H1 FY27 print (Feb-2027) showing the pre-sale book not rebuilding toward $100m+, a Sunfield quash (bear FY29-31 lower, plus an inventory impairment), or a Sunfield win with stage 1 titles (bull FY29-31 higher).
deliberately_unchanged.mid_cycle_npat_32m: Unchanged: six-year FY21-26 mean; nothing in the FY26 CSV row changes the history it is computed from.
deliberately_unchanged.dividend_payout_paths: Unchanged: base 40% from FY28 is $5.6m on $14m NPAT, trivially funded from $38.8m cash. Would move on: the Board resuming or formally deferring dividends at the FY27 results.
deliberately_unchanged.exit_multiples: Unchanged (0.55x/0.80x/1.05x P/B; 8x/11x/13x P/E): they price the FY31 governance and cycle state, not FY27 volumes. Would move on: a permanent CEO appointment and minority-protection outcome (up) or a further majority-holder dispute (down).
deliberately_unchanged.cost_of_equity_15_5pct: Unchanged: rf, ERP, size and governance premia are as at the v1.0 build the same day.
deliberately_unchanged.weights_30_50_20: Unchanged: the FY27 gap is now inside every scenario's path, so it is not double-charged through the weights.
deliberately_unchanged.share_count: Unchanged at 296.614m (CSV SharesOutstanding); options remain far out of the money.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
